text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Vilnius prosecutor's office started a case against former top officials of the Bank of Lithuania, accused of poor banking sector supervision and fraud.
- The tax inspection imposed a four million litas fine on Impar company for destroying documents of last year and refusing documents to officials.
- Official list company Medienos Plaushas intends to give shareholders the chance to convert around 30 percent of its shares into global depository receipts (GDRs).
- Tuesday marked the ninth anniversary of the formation of the Sajudis group, which went on to help dismantle Soviet rule in Lithuania.
- Parliament is expected to vote for the law on giving land back to people who owned it before Lithuania was annexed by the former Soviet Union.
- A new Klaipeda to Stockholm ferry route will be opened on June 10.
- Pope John Paul II said that a new wall of spiritual alienation is harming the European integration process.

- Shareholders of one of the biggest entertainment centres in the Baltic countries, Max'o Entertainment, are to decide on Wednesday on the company's future after the government imposed a big fine for trading with contraband alcohol.
- Swedish Modern Times Group, which acquired the commercial TELE 3 television group, will start broadcasting on June 8.
- Estonia's Hansa Asset Management plans to open an office in Vilnius before the end of the year.
- Lithuanian Gas continues negotiations with Merrill Lynch over a $25 million credit. The sum is needed to increase its working capital during the summer.
